matches.quote: Charge transfer dopes both layers ... and can produce metallicity whatever the magnetic order... none of these alternatives is excluded experimentally.
Total thickness: 1SIO/2SRO is 3 u.c. and 2SIO/2SRO is 4 u.c. ... at or above the single-film critical thicknesses ... add matched-thickness single-film references
Reference films: the AFM order of the 2-u.c. single films is taken from DFT and the literature. No magnetization data are shown for 2SIO or 2SRO.
There is no M(T) to establish Tc, and no link is shown between the ρ(T) kinks at 102 to 123 K and a magnetic transition.
Coherent weight: the claimed increase from 2SIO/1SRO to 1SIO/2SRO is not evident in Fig. 3A.iii versus B.iii.
U = 5 eV with J_H = 0.15U ... is far above the values usually used... Report the U dependence of the gap and the magnetic ground state
Add the in-plane versus out-of-plane loops that support the stated easy axis. Add the anomalous Hall effect, which would directly tie the ferromagnetism to the conducting layer.
There is no structural or chemical characterization: no STEM/EELS, XRD or X-ray reflectivity, and the RHEED oscillations and LEED patterns mentioned in Methods are not shown.
Intermixing: Ir/Ru interdiffusion over 1 to 2 u.c. would produce a SrIr1-xRuxO3 layer.

notes: C2 is marked partly because the review asks for matched-thickness single-film SRO references and notes weak ferromagnetism and capping/termination sensitivity (ref. 28) in ultrathin SRO, rather than directly framing the question around prior reports of metallic 1-2 u.c. SRO alone. C3 is marked partly because the review notes that spin configurations are asserted from DFT and structural data (STEM, XRD, LEED) are absent, but does not specifically ask for experimental measurement of the octahedral distortions. C5 is marked partly because the review challenges the causal link between magnetism and the IMT and asks for M(T) to compare with the 102-123 K transport kinks, without explicitly making the Slater-transition argument that metallicity persists above Tc. C10 is marked partly because P19 questions the visual evidence for the coherent-peak weight trend across samples and asks for fit uncertainties, which leads to quantifying the coherent weight.
